Title: Hawaiian Volcanoes
Content: The Hawaiian Islands are found in the Pacific Ocean. They were formed by a group of volcanoes located on the ocean floor. The islands are different ages because of how they formed.
Map `1` shows the locations and ages of the biggest islands that make up the Hawaiian Islands.
Kilauea is an active volcano on the island of Hawaii. It has been erupting since `text(1983)`.

Kilauea releases `text(two)` kinds of lava. Kilauea's quieter eruptions release a slow-moving lava called “pahoehoe.” When it cools, pahoehoe forms smooth rocks. Kilauea's loud, explosive eruptions release a fast-moving lava called “a'a.” When it cools, a'a forms rocks with sharp edges.
